step.name: ShellCheck - bootstrap/
step.run:
shellcheck -S warning bootstrap.sh
shellcheck -S warning bootstrap/lib/*.sh

step.name: Validate YAML configs with Python
step.run:
pip install pyyaml==6.0.2
exit_code=0
for f in configs/claude/config/*.yml; do
  echo "Validating $f ..."
  python3 -c "import sys, yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(sys.argv[1]))" "$f" || exit_code=1
done
if [ "$exit_code" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "YAML validation failed"
else
  echo "All YAML configs valid"
fi
exit $exit_code

step.name: Verify docs/COMMANDS.md is up-to-date with skills
step.run:
if ! configs/claude/scripts/generate_commands_doc.py --check; then
  echo ""
  echo "FAIL: docs/COMMANDS.md is out of sync with .apm/skills/."
  echo "Run 'configs/claude/scripts/generate_commands_doc.py' and commit the result."
  exit 1
fi
echo "docs/COMMANDS.md is up-to-date"

step.name: Verify bootstrap-free plugin release projections
step.run:
set -euo pipefail
uv run python tools/generate_plugin_views.py --check
uv run python tools/vendor_bundle_dependencies.py --check
uv run python tools/check_plugin_runtime_paths.py --json
# Agent-frontmatter gate: a bare `agent: name` silently resolves to
# general-purpose once skills are plugin-scoped, so it must be
# namespaced `plugin:agent`. Wired here rather than left as an
# opt-in utility -- a checker nothing runs closes nothing.
uv run python tools/check_agent_frontmatter.py
uv run python tools/render_capability_inventory.py --check
uv run python tools/render_plugin_capability_matrix.py --check \
  --inspection tests/fixtures/plugin_capability_inspection.json

step.name: Build and checksum coordinator wheel
step.run:
set -euo pipefail
rm -rf dist
uv build
shasum -a 256 dist/*

# (the source of truth). Without -L, find does not traverse the symlink.
SKILL_COUNT=$(find -L configs/claude/skills -name 'SKILL.md' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
echo "Found $SKILL_COUNT skills:"
find -L configs/claude/skills -name 'SKILL.md' | sed 's|/SKILL.md||;s|configs/claude/skills/||' | sort | sed 's/^/  /'
echo ""

echo "=== Scripts ==="

# This was `-lt 10`, which is not a gate: a bundle silently losing 17
# skills during the plugin move stays green, and so does any accident
# that drops 98 of them. Both sides of a `-lt` floor are derived from
# the same tree, so it can only ever confirm the tree agrees with
# itself. The global catalog expected_total lives in skill_policies.yml
# precisely because the move cannot edit it -- a PR that legitimately
# adds or removes a skill must change that integer in the same commit.
EXPECTED=$(sed -n 's/^expected_total:[[:space:]]*\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p' \

  echo "      in configs/claude/config/skill_policies.yml in the same commit."
  exit 1

  exit 1

step.run:

REMOTE_REFS="$(git ls-remote --exit-code origin \
  "refs/tags/${VERSION}" "refs/tags/${VERSION}^{}")"
STATUS=$?

  git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
  git tag -a "$VERSION" -m "manifest-skills $VERSION"

  exit "$STATUS"
else
  TAG_COMMIT="$(awk '
    $2 ~ /\^\{\}$/ { peeled=$1 }
    $2 !~ /\^\{\}$/ { direct=$1 }

  ' <<<"$REMOTE_REFS")"

    echo "release tag ${VERSION} points to ${TAG_COMMIT}, expected ${GITHUB_SHA}" >&2

equivalence.evidence: shellcheck-py vendors the upstream shellcheck 0.11.0 binary unmodified and its console entry runs it with the exact argv pre-commit passes through, no transformation. Confirmed locally: `shellcheck --version` reports 0.11.0, matching the pinned command:shellcheck=0.11.0 identity the registry now uses for lint.shell.scripts, lint.shell.bootstrap and hook.shellcheck (all three previously also probed the redundant distribution:shellcheck-py=0.11.0.1 wrapper identity; dropped per the engines-not-wrappers rule). Fixture corpus exercised against the direct engine locally; wrapper-side (shellcheck-py console script) run is pending Phase 3 (C7, needs the provisioned python-env).

The wrapper repo's rev suffix ('-1') is its own packaging revision, not an shfmt version; the underlying engine is shfmt 3.13.1. The registry's hook.shfmt body (tools/project_checks/hooks.py:_shfmt) deliberately runs `-d` instead of the wrapper's `-w`: `-w` rewrites files in place, which the non-mutation rule forbids for a check body. This is a reviewed, intentional argv divergence (formatting flags `-i 4 -ci -sr -ln bash` are identical; only the write-vs-diff flag differs), not an unconfirmed equivalence gap. Reading the wrapper repo's `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml` at v3.13.1-1 to confirm it invokes the same shfmt binary is pending Phase 3 (C7, needs network); the engine identity and version pin are not blocked on that read.

yamllint is a pure-Python distribution; the pre-commit hook's entry IS the same `yamllint` console script the registry probes for identity.
